summary:
I reviewed the builder's Descent 3 1.4 pilot patch adversarially and the core diagnosis holds. The staged pilot Descent3/sdf.plt (1770 B, md5 b03f1b0f19e6d430f3d64b8c426f4da6, version 0x2A) saves its game window as 640x480 in the dwords at 0x1F/0x23 (bytes 80020000e0010000). When the game enters flight (SM_GAME), it sizes the 3D view from those two values, and InitGameScreen then clamps them to the display. The staged value therefore gives a 640x480 box on a 1920x1080 display. Writing 4096x4096 there (bytes 0010000000100000) is correct on every box, because the clamp turns it into each box's own mode.

The built file (md5 a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849, 1770 B) differs from the original only inside 0x1F..0x26. It differs from the test pilot proven full screen on .240 (rvw.plt, run with -pilot RVW -Width 1920 -Height 1080) only in the 3 name bytes. I re-derived all of this myself from the share, the hardware screenshots and log, and the GPL source.

I fixed four real defects in apply.py and the test file:
(1) The test did `import apply` through sys.path, and so does test_patch_idtech2.py. In one pytest process, which is how tests/run_all.sh runs, each test got the other's module in both orders. The descent3 test now loads its module under its own name.
(2) --build refused to run once the share held the patched pilot, so the patch was not reproducible after publishing. It now rebuilds the original by reverting the 8 bytes and checking the original md5.
(3) "patched" matched any 0x2A pilot that had 4096x4096 at 0x1F. It now requires the file to revert exactly to the original.
(4) --publish did not check its local inputs, and did not re-read each file it put. It now does both, and it also adds a missing backup when the live file is already patched.

I corrected one major point in the launcher hand-off. The builder's proposed stage-fleetres.py change (editing only the recipe's replacement text) would do nothing and report nothing: patch_launcher skips any launcher that already calls FLEETRES.BAT, which the staged 'Play Descent 3.bat' does. I proved this with the stager's own code on a scratch copy. The change has to be a "fix" (repair) pair; that is also simulated. I also corrected several claims: title-level disc_mount no longer affects .123, since all four LCD boxes now report a mounter; the hardware plan's menu keys were wrong from a fresh main menu; and the tests/README.md row and the _deploy_generation.txt bump were missing.

--check and --build ran, and building twice gives the same md5. --publish was only exercised with --dry-run. Nothing was written to the share or to any box.
launcher_changes_needed: scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py, TITLES['Descent3']: this CORRECTS the builder's instruction, which would silently do nothing. Changing only the rec() replacement string never reaches the staged launcher. patch_launcher() returns at `if MARK in body`, and the staged 'Play Descent 3.bat' (2760 B, md5 3dd6cb024545a5964e32ef16d347047a) already contains `call "%~dp0FLEETRES.BAT"`. Run with the stager's own Runner on a scratch copy, it gives skipped=1, no error, file unchanged, and --check stays green (build-descent3/review/launcher-mechanism-sim.log). The repo's own test_a_changed_recipe_can_still_reach_an_already_staged_launcher documents exactly this trap. Do BOTH of the following. (a) Set the rec replacement to 'start "" "%~dp0main.exe" -launched -pilot SDF -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%', so that a launcher rebuilt from scratch gets the new line directly. (b) Add the repair pair, which is what reaches the staged file: "fix": {"Play Descent 3.bat": [('start "" "%~dp0main.exe" -launched -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%', 'start "" "%~dp0main.exe" -launched -pilot SDF -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%')]}. Simulated results: --check fails before shipping with 'still has ...'; repair() takes the file from 2760 to 2771 B and keeps CRLF (50 CRLF, 0 bare LF); a second run skips; --check afterwards is clean. The old string is not a substring of the new one, so nothing is inserted twice, and the line has no parentheses. Shipping it headless: LIB_DEFAULT is the read-only /mnt mount and gvfs is not mounted, so apply the same Runner.repair() to a scratch copy, put that ONE file with scripts/fleet/sharewrite.py put, and check that `stage-fleetres.py --check` reports nothing for Descent3. The size changes, so GAMESYNC recopies the launcher whatever its mtime. Why the switch is needed: without -pilot, the staged launcher stops at the PILOTS dialog (195_d3_after_esc.png; menu.cpp MainMenu calls PilotSelect whenever no -pilot/+name is given). A pilot the player creates there gets the Video-menu slot size, 640x480 (pilot::initialize). -pilot keeps mission progress and binds, because read_mission_data hard-codes skip=false. Add in the same commit: 'Descent3' in the tuple of tests/python/test_fleetres_staging.py::test_a_changed_recipe_can_still_reach_an_already_staged_launcher; a test that both the Descent3 rec replacement and its fix pair carry '-pilot SDF' on the main.exe line; and a share-side test, skipping loudly, that the shipped launcher's main.exe line reads '-launched -pilot SDF -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%'. Optional: -nointro, which the Join launcher already passes.

'Join Descent 3 - LAN.bat' (hand-written in the library, no generator; there is no Descent3 disc-mount spec either): NO change. It already runs main.exe -launched -nointro -pilot SDF -directip +connect %HOSTIP% -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%. With the patched pilot the join also renders full screen.

'Host Descent 3 - LAN.bat': NO change. main.exe -dedicated never reads or writes a pilot: PltReadFile builds an in-memory 'SERVER' pilot and PltWriteFile returns early when Dedicated_server (pilot.cpp). It has no 3D window.

agent/shared/gameres.h and provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c: NO change, and no GAMERES row. The pilot is binary and not per box, since InitGameScreen clamps 4096 to each display. A GAMERES writer would fight the game's own rewrite of sdf.plt at the first mission, and '0 value(s) changed' would never hold. This patch touches no file that FLEETRES and GAMERES both write, so the identical-bytes rule does not come into it.

Delivery. After apply.py --publish (and the launcher repair), bump Files/Games-Library/_deploy_generation.txt ONCE for the whole lcd1080 lane, after every lane has published. The current line is '2026-09-28 staged icons XP-drawable ...'; the first non-blank, non-# line is the generation. Write it last with sharewrite.py and verify it through /mnt. Without the bump no provisioned box re-syncs Descent3: the startup GAMESYNC idles on gamesync.done, and autodeploy runs RESET+START only when the generation changes.

tests/README.md, a shared index file: check the other worktrees with `git -C <wt> status --short` first, per CLAUDE.md. tests/python/test_readme_lists_every_test.py currently FAILS for test_patch_descent3.py and for 9 other new files. Add to the 'Fix -> test coverage' table: | Descent 3 1.4: -Width/-Height gave a 1920x1080 display but the 3D view stayed a 640x480 box - SM_GAME sizes the view from the pilot's saved game_window_w/h, clamped by InitGameScreen, and the staged sdf.plt saved 640x480; the pilot now carries 4096x4096, proven full screen on .240 (.195/.240, 2026-09-29) | `provisioning/patches/descent3/apply.py` -> `Games-Library/Descent3/sdf.plt` | `python/test_patch_descent3.py` |

Library docs, fix phase, following the staged-game loop. requires.json: dropping the title-level "requires_capabilities": ["disc_mount"] is HYGIENE, not a blocker for this lane. Correction to the builder: .123 now reports disc_mount=true (d347bus), as do .145/.240 (d347bus) and .195 (BazisVirtualCDBus), per the share's fleet-inventory JSONs of 2026-09-28 23:39-23:47. Descent 3 is therefore not suppressed on any of the four LCD boxes today. It would still hide all three shortcuts on a box with no mounter (SCHEMA rule 7). Also drop the 'relative mouse deltas / not automatable' note (refuted on .195/.240), and bump requirements_version. README-FLEET.txt: the same correction, plus the pilot-window cause. provisioning/fleetres/PER-TITLE-STATUS.md row 'Descent3 | 1080p | main.exe -Width/-Height' must say 1080p needs BOTH the switches AND the staged sdf.plt with its game window at 4096x4096. CLAUDE.md's keyboard-navigable triage table lists Descent 3 under 'Relative-mouse menu - not automatable'; that is refuted (.195/.240, arrows+Enter+Escape+'=') and it belongs in the keyboard-navigable row. Add a FINDINGS entry.

Optional, not the default: -aspect 1.78 on 16:9 panels. It fixes the 1.33x stretch but zooms the vertical axis, cuts the vertical FOV and pushes the cockpit monitors off the bottom of the screen (measured on .240); that is a taste call. RS_bitdepth=32 in install.reg is cosmetic.
risks: The game rewrites sdf.plt on each box at the first mission start: version 0x2A->0x2B, 1770->1772 B, and it saves the CLAMPED size (1920x1080 on an LCD, the tube's mode on a CRT), not 4096. If that box later gets a bigger display, the view stays at the saved size until GAMESYNC recopies the staged pilot or the player presses '='. Hardware moves between boxes on this fleet, so this can happen.

Shipping this fix overwrites played pilots once. After the generation bump, every box whose sdf.plt the game already rewrote (1772 B) gets the staged file back, and the mission progress and binds stored in that pilot are lost. There is no way around it: a box whose rewritten pilot saved 640x480 keeps the small box until that file is replaced. Any later sync over the title does the same, both before and after this patch.

Delivery depends on the mtime. GAMESYNC skips a file only when the size matches AND the mtime is within 2 s (agent/shared/gsresume.h). The patched pilot is the same size (1770 B) as the original, so it reaches boxes that hold the original only because its mtime differs; sharewrite.py enforces a fresh one. If sharewrite ever exits 4 (stale stamp), the file IS on the share with the right bytes and apply.py stops loudly; re-run --publish, which then skips the already-patched file.

The patch is proven only on pilot version 0x2A and on this exact file. apply.py refuses anything else. --check fails on any unknown *.plt, and a staged pilot that carries 4096x4096 but differs elsewhere is reported unknown, never patched.

The PILOTS-dialog path with the patched pilot is proven by source only: pilot::verify() never touches the game window. The hardware test used -pilot RVW. Until the launcher repair ships, 'Play Descent 3.bat' goes through that dialog, so the hardware plan tests that path explicitly.

Proportions: at full screen the 4:3 projection is stretched 1.33x on 16:9 (rend_GetAspectRatio assumes 4:3). The fix makes 1080p usable; it does not make the image Hor+. -aspect 1.78 has measured side effects.

The in-game Video > Resolution menu still lists only 7 hardcoded 4:3 modes. Picking one sets force_res_change, overrides -Width/-Height for the session, and the pilot then saves that size. 1080p comes from the launcher, never from the menu.

If only the builder's launcher instruction were applied (edit the rec replacement), Play Descent 3.bat would never get -pilot SDF and stage-fleetres.py --check would stay green: the project's 'reported success' failure shape. The corrected 'fix' pair avoids it.

Test hygiene outside this area: tests/python/test_patch_idtech2.py still imports its module as a bare `apply` through sys.path. Any future patch test that does the same will collide with it in tests/run_all.sh. Flag this to the idtech2 reviewer.
Do not use .124 for the CRT check. It carries the V5 6000 on vcr-kmd, D3's Direct3D path there is untested, and mode switches on its 1998 CRT must be paced. Use .143 or .133.
hw_verification_plan:
FUTURE only; nothing below was done in this phase.

Preconditions:
- (a) apply.py --publish has run. The backup _patches/Descent3/originals-2026-09-29/sdf.plt is b03f1b0f..., and the live Descent3/sdf.plt is a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849; both verified through /mnt.
- (b) The stage-fleetres.py 'fix' pair has shipped: 'Play Descent 3.bat' is 2771 B and its main.exe line reads '-launched -pilot SDF -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%'.
- (c) ONE _deploy_generation.txt bump has been made, or GAMESYNC RESET+START is run by hand on the test box.

Test boxes: .240 (XP, X800) first, then .195 (Win7), .123 and .145.

1. Purge per the staged-game loop.
   - taskkill /f /im "main.exe" (quoted).
   - Read the title's destination from GAMESYNC STATUS 'dest' (C:\Games unless GamesDir is set).
   - rd /s /q "<dest>\Descent3", then DIRLIST to prove it is gone.
   - Delete the three desktop .lnk files: 'Descent 3', 'Descent 3 - Host LAN Server', 'Descent 3 - Join LAN Game'.
2. Redeploy and check the post-conditions.
   - GAMESYNC RESET, then GAMESYNC START, then poll GAMESYNC STATUS until state=done AND failed_files=0 AND titles_done=titles_total AND titles_total equals the library's count for this box's profile.
   - DOWNLOAD <dest>\Descent3\sdf.plt: md5 must be a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849 and bytes 0x1F..0x26 must be 0010000000100000.
   - DOWNLOAD 'Play Descent 3.bat': 2771 B, with the -pilot SDF line.
3. Launch through the agent.
   - EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "<dest>\Descent3" "Play Descent 3.bat"
   - WINLIST: 'foreground' must be the 'Descent 3' window before any UIKEY.
   - UIKEY ESCAPE (repeat as needed) skips the intro.
   - SCREENSHOT: it must show the MAIN MENU with NEW GAME highlighted and NO PILOTS dialog. If PILOTS appears, the launcher repair did not ship.
4. From that fresh main menu press RETURN (New Game), DOWN (Pilot Training), RETURN. This is the sequence measured on .240 at 01:12:44. The builder's 'UP x3' is only right after returning from Options and is wrong from a fresh menu. Take a screenshot before each RETURN.
5. After about 25 s:
   - DISPLAYCFG get must read 1920x1080 on the LCD boxes. On .145 cross-check the 'Descent 3' WINLIST rect 0,0-1920,1080, because DISPLAYCFG there reads the inactive Intel HD.
   - SCREENSHOT 0: the non-black bbox must be 0,0-1920,1080; unpatched it is 640,300-1280,780. GDI captures this title on XP and on Win7 .195.
   - Record the fullscreen result in the compat matrix.
6. Prove the PILOTS-dialog path, which is proven by source only so far.
   - taskkill /f /im "main.exe".
   - Restore the staged pilot: copy /y "\\192.168.1.122\files\Files\Games-Library\Descent3\sdf.plt" "<dest>\Descent3\sdf.plt", then check md5 a4293.... The first run rewrote it to 0x2B with 1920x1080 saved, which would pass for the wrong reason.
   - EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "<dest>\Descent3" main.exe -launched -Width 1920 -Height 1080 (no -pilot). RETURN at PILOTS (SDF), then New Game > Pilot Training. It must also fill 1920x1080.
7. Repeat once on a CRT box, .143 or .133 (not .124). Pace launches at least 5 s apart. The view must fill that box's own FLEETRES mode.
8. What must NOT change:
   - Host LAN on box A: the dedicated server logs 'Opening level' and netstat shows TCP+UDP 2092 LISTENING.
   - Join LAN from box B (lanhost.txt or the first argument) reaches A's game and renders full screen. Take screenshots of BOTH boxes, per the LAN proof rule.
   - The dev-host descent3-server still answers (gameservers.py). It has its own tree, and its sdf.plt md5 is b03f1b0f....
   - The Video > Resolution list is still the 7 hardcoded 4:3 modes.
   - GAMERES APPLY on the box still reports 0 value(s) changed.
9. Clean up.
   - taskkill /f /im "main.exe".
   - Delete <dest>\Descent3\custom\cache\d3s*.tmp and .lock.
   - Confirm the desktop is back at its persisted mode; a killed D3 can leave it at 640x480.
   - Expect the box's sdf.plt to be 1772 B, version 0x2B, with the clamped size saved. That is the game's normal rewrite: record it, do not restore it.
10. Push to every other connected box. The generation bump does RESET+START once per box. On each box, DOWNLOAD sdf.plt (md5 a4293... until it is played) and 'Play Descent 3.bat', and take a fullscreen in-flight screenshot on every LCD box (.123, .145, .195, .240).
review_notes:
WHAT I VERIFIED, INDEPENDENTLY OF THE BUILDER'S REPORT

Staged tree
- The only *.plt in the staged Descent3 tree is sdf.plt (1770 B, md5 b03f1b0f...). There is none in _patches either. Both searches used find -iname.

Header, decoded by hand
- 0x00 version 0x2A
- 0x04 'sdf'; 0x08 'Pyro-GL'; 0x10-0x14 five empty strings
- 0x15 picture_id FFFF; then difficulty 01, profanity 00, audiotaunts 01
- 0x1A hud_mode 02; hud_stat 0x0040; graphical 0x3FBE
- 0x1F = 640 and 0x23 = 480, i.e. bytes 80020000e0010000
- This matches the read order in pilot_class.cpp (read_custom_multiplayer_data ends with picture_id).

Build output
- The output is md5 a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849.
- cmp -l against the original: only offsets 0x1F, 0x20, 0x23 and 0x24 differ.
- cmp -l against the hardware-proven rvw.plt: only the 3 name bytes differ.

Hardware evidence
- 240_d3_1080_ingame.png: the 640x480 box.
- 240_d3_rvw_ingame_noaspect.png: full 1920x1080.
- commands.log 01:12:18: `-pilot RVW -Width 1920 -Height 1080`, bbox 0,0-1920,1080.
- 195_d3_after_esc.png: the staged launcher stops at PILOTS.
- The .240 run without -pilot reached the main menu only because it went through the verifier's own _review_d3.bat. That file was 147 B and has been deleted; its contents were never recorded.

Source (GPL, fetched to build-descent3/review/src)
- InitGameScreen clamps the requested size to the display, and SM_GAME stores the clamped size back into the pilot.
- PltReadFile and PltWriteFile both return early when Dedicated_server, so the dedicated server never touches sdf.plt and --install-server is not relevant. The Wine descent3-server keeps its own original copy in ~/descent3-server.
- PilotSelect goes through VerifyPilotData, and pilot::verify() leaves the window alone.
- The -pilot X switch loads X.plt; without it the PILOTS dialog always opens.
- read_mission_data always reads the mission data.

Other checks
- sharewrite.py's interface matches the call in apply.py.
- GAMESYNC's resume rule (gsresume.h): skip only when the size matches and the mtime is within 2 s.
- The disc_mount state of each box comes from the share's inventory JSONs.
- Only our code is under provisioning/patches/descent3. The builder's git-ignored __pycache__ was removed, and game bytes live only in ~/.retro-fleet/patch-out/descent3.
- Nothing was written to the share or to any box. The share md5s are unchanged: sdf.plt b03f1b0f..., 'Play Descent 3.bat' 3dd6cb02....

WHAT I CHANGED (apply.py and test_patch_descent3.py)

1. Test collision
- The builder's test did sys.path.insert plus `import apply`, and test_patch_idtech2.py does the same.
- tests/run_all.sh runs a single pytest process, and both orders failed.
- The test now loads the module through importlib as 'descent3_apply'; the pair passes in both orders (63 passed).

2. --build is now idempotent across the whole lifecycle
- Before, it refused to run once the share held the patched pilot.
- Now it rebuilds the original by reverting the 8 bytes, asserts the original md5, and produces the same output.
- The manifest records 'built_from' and 'rel'.

3. 'patched' is strict
- The file must revert to the recorded original md5.
- The two pilots the game rewrote on .195/.240, and rvw.plt, are all correctly 'unknown'.

4. --publish hardening
- Before any put, it proves that the local patched file and the local original match the manifest AND that the patched file equals patch_pilot(original).
- It re-reads every put through /mnt, so a write gvfs silently dropped is caught.
- It creates a missing backup even when the live file is already patched.
- It flushes its command line before the child's output, and fails cleanly when sharewrite.py is absent.

5. --check reports the backup state once the share is patched: FAIL for a wrong backup, WARN for a missing one.

6. parse_pilot raises PilotError, not struct.error or IndexError, on any truncation inside the header.

7. Pinned constants
- PILOTS records patched_md5, which is asserted on every build.
- HW_VERIFIED pins the rvw.plt md5 proven on .240.
- A share test proves that the build output, renamed to 'rvw', is exactly that file.

8. --dry-run is rejected unless --publish is given, and an unmounted library gives a clear FAIL.

CORRECTIONS TO THE BUILDER'S REPORT
- The launcher mechanism, which is the major item: see launcher_changes_needed[0], and the simulation in build-descent3/review/launcher-mechanism-sim.log.
- The claim that disc_mount suppresses Descent 3 on .123 is stale.
- The hardware plan's 'UP x3' is wrong from a fresh menu; the plan also lacked the dialog-path proof, the GamesDir dest, and the advice to avoid .124.
- The deploy-generation bump and the tests/README.md row were missing.
- The concern about a doubled insertion was moot, because patch_launcher never re-runs a sub on a staged launcher.

CONFIRMED UNCHANGED
- The patch bytes, the offsets, the 4096x4096 value, the Join and Host verdicts, the 'no GAMERES row' verdict, and the proportions caveat.
